# dpbequ

> Compute diagonal scaling factors for a symmetric band matrix.

<section class="intro">

Computes `S[i]=1/sqrt(A[i,i])`, `SCOND=sqrt(min(A[i,i]))/sqrt(max(A[i,i]))` and `AMAX=max(A[i,i])` for positive selected diagonals. The input band matrix is unchanged. Scalar `INFO` reports the first nonpositive diagonal; positive diagonals alone do not establish positive definiteness or numerical stability. These interfaces and support restrictions remain proposed package adaptations.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var dpbequ = require( '@stdlib/lapack/base/dpbequ' );
```

#### dpbequ( order, uplo, N, KD, AB, LDAB, S, SCOND, AMAX )

Writes scaling factors and two scalar outputs and returns numeric `INFO`.

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

var AB = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 16.0, 64.0 ] );
var S = new Float64Array( 3 );
var SCOND = new Float64Array( 1 );
var AMAX = new Float64Array( 1 );
var info = dpbequ( 'column-major', 'lower', 3, 0, AB, 1, S, SCOND, AMAX );
// returns 0
// S => <Float64Array>[ 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 ]
// SCOND => <Float64Array>[ 0.25 ]
// AMAX => <Float64Array>[ 64 ]
```

-   **order**: `'row-major'` (`101`) or `'column-major'` (`102`).
-   **uplo**: `'upper'` (`121`) or `'lower'` (`122`); character selectors `'U'` and `'L'` are rejected.
-   **N**, **KD**: nonnegative primitive safe integers, at most `2147483646`.
-   **AB**: read-only intrinsic `Float64Array` containing the full `H`-by-`N` compact band view, `H=KD+1`.
-   **LDAB**: primitive safe integer leading dimension; column-major requires `LDAB>=H`, row-major `LDAB>=max(1,N)`.
-   **S**: output-only intrinsic `Float64Array` with `N` active scaling cells.
-   **SCOND**, **AMAX**: mutable intrinsic `Float64Array` scalar outputs at index zero.

For zero-based `i,j`, upper storage places `A(i,j)` in band row `KD+i-j`, lower in row `i-j`. Band cell `b,j` is `AB[b*LDAB+j]` row-major or `AB[b+j*LDAB]` column-major. Upper diagonals are in row `KD`, lower in row zero. `KD>=N` is supported. Only selected diagonals are numerically read, but the entire conservative `H`-by-`N` view is validated, including unused cells and padding envelopes.

<!-- lint disable maximum-heading-length -->

#### dpbequ.ndarray( uplo, N, KD, AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB, S, strideS, offsetS, SCOND, offsetSCOND, AMAX, offsetAMAX )

Uses independent signed element strides and offsets relative to the actual typed-array views.

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );

var AB = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, -0.0, 16.0, 25.0 ] );
var S = new Float64Array( 4 );
var SCOND = new Float64Array( [ -7.0 ] );
var AMAX = new Float64Array( [ -9.0 ] );
var info = dpbequ.ndarray( 'lower', 4, 0, AB, 1, 1, 0, S, 1, 0, SCOND, 0, AMAX, 0 );
// returns 2
// S => <Float64Array>[ 4, -0, 16, 25 ]
// SCOND => <Float64Array>[ -7 ]
// AMAX => <Float64Array>[ 25 ]
```

Band cell `b,j` is `AB[offsetAB+b*strideAB1+j*strideAB2]`; output cell `j` is `S[offsetS+j*strideS]`. Scalar cells are `SCOND[offsetSCOND]` and `AMAX[offsetAMAX]`. Metadata must be primitive safe integers; active offsets are nonnegative. Full views must fit, be injective and have exactly representable products, corners and indexed byte sums. Used zero strides are rejected. Valid unused singleton strides need not enter arithmetic.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   All selected diagonals must be finite before any output write. Ignored band or padding entries may be nonfinite; no full-value scan is performed. This finite-diagonal restriction is a proposed deviation from Reference-LAPACK.
-   `INFO=0` writes all scaling factors and both scalar results. For positive `INFO`, every original selected diagonal is copied into `S`, `AMAX` includes all columns, and `SCOND` retains the caller's exact sentinel. `INFO` is the first one-based nonpositive diagonal, including negative zero. Failure is not a partial early diagonal copy.
-   Strict comparisons retain the first tied extremum. On mixed negative/positive zero failures, the first zero sign is retained in `AMAX`; sampled GNU reference builds instead retain the last zero sign. No universal signed-zero, nonfinite or untested-platform bitwise parity is claimed.
-   All four active conservative indexed byte envelopes must be pairwise disjoint, even though only the input diagonal is read. Disjoint envelopes may share one ordinary backing buffer. Overlapping gaps or unused band cells are still rejected; inputs are not copied to evade aliases.
-   Active views require intrinsic `Float64Array` over ordinary `ArrayBuffer`, including current in-bounds resizable extents. Shared backing, cloned shared storage, proxies, detached and current out-of-bounds views are rejected. Captured intrinsics ignore shadowed metadata and support genuine crossrealm views and subclasses.
-   Backing must remain stable and exclusive until synchronous return: no resize, detach, transfer, reentry or concurrent foreign mutation. Pure JavaScript cannot detect physical overlap between externally fabricated ordinary buffers with different identities; callers must guarantee physical disjointness. Native/C independently reject physical indexed-envelope overlaps, and these errors propagate without fallback.
-   For `N=0`, validate selectors, dimensions, main `LDAB`, and only active `SCOND`/`AMAX` storage, offsets and mutual disjointness. Write `SCOND=1` and positive-zero `AMAX` and return zero. `AB`, `S` and their unused ndarray metadata are not inspected. Main leading-dimension bounds still apply.
-   Native eligibility uses conservative signed32 metadata, products and corners before dispatch. Otherwise valid wider metadata uses the JavaScript kernel before mutation. Backend errors never trigger a retry after mutation. There is no numerical BLAS dependency, integer output staging or heap workspace; internal Node-API allocation is not a transactional engine-wide allocation guarantee.
-   Invalid selectors, array brands or backing throw `TypeError`; invalid integer metadata, geometry, aliases or selected nonfinite diagonals throw `RangeError` before routine-owned writes. Type annotations cannot encode these runtime preconditions.
-   The proposed Node engine floor is a feature/support declaration. Actual package execution uses Node24/Linux and does not certify Node16, other engines, native platforms or arbitrary toolchains.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```javascript
'use strict';

// MODULES //

var assert = require( 'assert' );
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );
var dpbequ = require( '@stdlib/lapack/base/dpbequ' );


// MAIN //

// Only selected diagonals are read; ignored band entries may be nonfinite:
var AB = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 16.0, 64.0, NaN, Infinity, 999.0 ] );
var S = new Float64Array( 3 );
var SCOND = new Float64Array( [ -7.0 ] );
var AMAX = new Float64Array( [ -9.0 ] );
var info = dpbequ( 'row-major', 'lower', 3, 1, AB, 3, S, SCOND, AMAX );
assert.strictEqual( info, 0 );
assert.strictEqual( Array.prototype.join.call( S, ',' ), '0.5,0.25,0.125' );
assert.strictEqual( SCOND[ 0 ], 0.25 );
assert.strictEqual( AMAX[ 0 ], 64.0 );
assert.strictEqual( S[ 0 ]*S[ 0 ]*AB[ 0 ], 1.0 );
assert.strictEqual( S[ 1 ]*S[ 1 ]*AB[ 1 ], 1.0 );
assert.strictEqual( S[ 2 ]*S[ 2 ]*AB[ 2 ], 1.0 );
console.log( 'INFO: %d; S: %s; SCOND: %d; AMAX: %d', info, Array.prototype.join.call( S, ', ' ), SCOND[ 0 ], AMAX[ 0 ] );

// Signed band/output strides and scalar offsets retain all guards:
AB = new Float64Array( [ 8.0, 64.0, 999.0, 16.0, 999.0, 4.0, 999.0, 8.0 ] );
S = new Float64Array( [ 7.0, 7.0, 7.0, 7.0, 7.0 ] );
SCOND = new Float64Array( [ 7.0, -7.0, 7.0 ] );
AMAX = new Float64Array( [ 7.0, -9.0, 7.0 ] );
info = dpbequ.ndarray( 'upper', 3, 1, AB, 1, -2, 4, S, -1, 3, SCOND, 1, AMAX, 1 );
assert.strictEqual( info, 0 );
assert.strictEqual( Array.prototype.join.call( S, ',' ), '7,0.125,0.25,0.5,7' );
assert.strictEqual( Array.prototype.join.call( SCOND, ',' ), '7,0.25,7' );
assert.strictEqual( Array.prototype.join.call( AMAX, ',' ), '7,64,7' );
assert.strictEqual( Array.prototype.join.call( AB, ',' ), '8,64,999,16,999,4,999,8' );
console.log( 'Strided INFO: %d; guarded S: %s', info, Array.prototype.join.call( S, ', ' ) );

// Failure copies every diagonal and finds AMAX even in later columns:
AB = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, -0.0, 16.0, 25.0 ] );
S = new Float64Array( 4 );
SCOND = new Float64Array( [ -0.0 ] );
AMAX = new Float64Array( [ -9.0 ] );
info = dpbequ( 'column-major', 'lower', 4, 0, AB, 1, S, SCOND, AMAX );
assert.strictEqual( info, 2 );
assert.strictEqual( Array.prototype.join.call( S, ',' ), '4,0,16,25' );
assert.strictEqual( 1/S[ 1 ], -Infinity );
assert.strictEqual( 1/SCOND[ 0 ], -Infinity );
assert.strictEqual( AMAX[ 0 ], 25.0 );
console.log( 'Failure INFO: %d; copied S: %s; AMAX: %d', info, Array.prototype.join.call( S, ', ' ), AMAX[ 0 ] );

// Strict-first AMAX preserves the first tied zero sign on failure:
AB = new Float64Array( [ -0.0, 0.0 ] );
S = new Float64Array( 2 );
info = dpbequ( 'row-major', 'lower', 2, 0, AB, 2, S, SCOND, AMAX );
assert.strictEqual( info, 1 );
assert.strictEqual( 1/AMAX[ 0 ], -Infinity );
assert.strictEqual( 1/SCOND[ 0 ], -Infinity );
console.log( 'Mixed-zero INFO: %d; first AMAX sign: %d', info, 1/AMAX[ 0 ] );

// Empty input ignores AB/S but validates and writes both active scalars:
info = dpbequ( 'column-major', 'upper', 0, 2, null, 3, null, SCOND, AMAX );
assert.strictEqual( info, 0 );
assert.strictEqual( SCOND[ 0 ], 1.0 );
assert.strictEqual( 1/AMAX[ 0 ], Infinity );
console.log( 'Empty INFO: %d; SCOND: %d; AMAX: %d', info, SCOND[ 0 ], AMAX[ 0 ] );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="c">

## C APIs

```c
#include "stdlib/lapack/base/dpbequ.h"
```

#### c_dpbequ( order, uplo, N, KD, AB, LDAB, S, SCOND, AMAX )

```c
LAPACK_INT API_SUFFIX(c_dpbequ)( const LAPACK_LAYOUT order, const int uplo, const LAPACK_INT N, const LAPACK_INT KD, const double *AB, const LAPACK_INT LDAB, double *S, double *SCOND, double *AMAX );
```

<!-- lint disable maximum-heading-length -->

#### c_dpbequ_ndarray( uplo, N, KD, AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB, S, strideS, offsetS, SCOND, offsetSCOND, AMAX, offsetAMAX )

```c
LAPACK_INT API_SUFFIX(c_dpbequ_ndarray)( const int uplo, const LAPACK_INT N, const LAPACK_INT KD, const double *AB, const LAPACK_INT strideAB1, const LAPACK_INT strideAB2, const LAPACK_INT offsetAB, double *S, const LAPACK_INT strideS, const LAPACK_INT offsetS, double *SCOND, const LAPACK_INT offsetSCOND, double *AMAX, const LAPACK_INT offsetAMAX );
```

Both return configured `LAPACK_INT` `INFO`; negative values identify prewrite argument errors (`-1` through `-9` main, `-1` through `-14` ndarray). Exact maps and validation precedence are documented in the public header. `LAPACK_ILP64` selects metadata width; API suffix configuration is independent. Raw `N/KD` are at most configured `MAX-1`; products, sums, magnitudes and physical byte envelopes cannot wrap. Minimum configured integer strides are rejected before negation on active calls. Caller storage must have sufficient capacity, double alignment and stable exclusive lifetime. Empty calls ignore input/vector pointers and inactive metadata but require two valid disjoint scalar cells. No numerical BLAS linkage is required.

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/lapack/base/dpbequ.h"
#include "stdlib/lapack/base/shared.h"
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

/**
* Main execution sequence.
*/
int main( void ) {
    const double AB[] = { 4.0, 16.0, 64.0, NAN, INFINITY, 999.0 };
    double before[ 6 ];
    const double B[] = { 8.0, 64.0, 999.0, 16.0, 999.0, 4.0, 999.0, 8.0 };
    double T[] = { 7.0, 7.0, 7.0, 7.0, 7.0 };
    double C[] = { 7.0, -7.0, 7.0 };
    double M[] = { 7.0, -9.0, 7.0 };
    const double F[] = { 4.0, -0.0, 16.0, 25.0 };
    const double Z[] = { -0.0, 0.0 };
    double S[ 4 ] = { 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 };
    double sc = -0.0;
    double am = -9.0;
    LAPACK_INT info;

    memcpy( before, AB, sizeof AB );
    info = API_SUFFIX(c_dpbequ)( LAPACK_ROW_MAJOR, LAPACK_LOWER_TRIANGLE, 3, 1, AB, 3, S, &sc, &am );
    if ( info != 0 || S[ 0 ] != 0.5 || S[ 1 ] != 0.25 || S[ 2 ] != 0.125 || sc != 0.25 || am != 64.0 || memcmp( before, AB, sizeof AB ) != 0 ) {
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if ( S[ 0 ]*S[ 0 ]*AB[ 0 ] != 1.0 || S[ 1 ]*S[ 1 ]*AB[ 1 ] != 1.0 || S[ 2 ]*S[ 2 ]*AB[ 2 ] != 1.0 ) {
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    printf( "INFO: %d; SCOND: %.2f; AMAX: %.1f\n", (int)info, sc, am );

    info = API_SUFFIX(c_dpbequ_ndarray)( LAPACK_UPPER_TRIANGLE, 3, 1, B, 1, -2, 4, T, -1, 3, C, 1, M, 1 );
    if ( info != 0 || T[ 0 ] != 7.0 || T[ 1 ] != 0.125 || T[ 2 ] != 0.25 || T[ 3 ] != 0.5 || T[ 4 ] != 7.0 || C[ 0 ] != 7.0 || C[ 1 ] != 0.25 || C[ 2 ] != 7.0 || M[ 0 ] != 7.0 || M[ 1 ] != 64.0 || M[ 2 ] != 7.0 ) {
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    printf( "Strided INFO: %d; guarded S: %.3f, %.2f, %.1f\n", (int)info, T[ 1 ], T[ 2 ], T[ 3 ] );

    sc = -0.0;
    info = API_SUFFIX(c_dpbequ)( LAPACK_COL_MAJOR, LAPACK_LOWER_TRIANGLE, 4, 0, F, 1, S, &sc, &am );
    if ( info != 2 || S[ 0 ] != 4.0 || S[ 1 ] != 0.0 || !signbit(S[ 1 ]) || S[ 2 ] != 16.0 || S[ 3 ] != 25.0 || sc != 0.0 || !signbit(sc) || am != 25.0 ) {
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    printf( "Failure INFO: %d; later-column AMAX: %.1f\n", (int)info, am );

    info = API_SUFFIX(c_dpbequ)( LAPACK_ROW_MAJOR, LAPACK_LOWER_TRIANGLE, 2, 0, Z, 2, S, &sc, &am );
    if ( info != 1 || am != 0.0 || !signbit(am) || sc != 0.0 || !signbit(sc) ) {
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    printf( "Mixed-zero INFO: %d; first AMAX sign retained\n", (int)info );

    info = API_SUFFIX(c_dpbequ)( LAPACK_COL_MAJOR, LAPACK_UPPER_TRIANGLE, 0, 2, NULL, 3, NULL, &sc, &am );
    if ( info != 0 || sc != 1.0 || am != 0.0 || signbit(am) ) {
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    printf( "Empty INFO: %d; SCOND: %.1f; AMAX: %.1f\n", (int)info, sc, am );
    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}
```
